label: copy-phase input d
explanation: Fires when the token d is fed back as input during the copy phase (t > L), i.e. the model just output d and now receives it. It never fires on d in the original phase or on any other input token (only 53 tiny stray activations on 0/w/f at the last copy steps, ~0% of mass). Precision is about 0.89: the non-firing d inputs are concentrated at the earliest copy positions (recall_idx 1-2). Restricting to recall_idx >= 3 gives precision 0.97 but loses a third of activations. The strongest examples are d inputs late in the copy phase of long sequences, and the lowest-quartile examples are d inputs early in the copy phase, so magnitude appears to grow with copy position. Output token, neighbouring tokens and digit count have little effect.

issues: All the factual claims check out on dev: the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phase (0 of 3.73M steps), d inputs carry 100% of the activation mass, and 53 stray activations on 0, f and w carry about 0% of the mass. On the test split the predicate scores P 0.888, R 0.999, F1 0.940, mass recall 1.000, which matches the reported numbers.

The false positives sit in the early copy positions. Precision for d inputs by recall_idx is 0.745 at 1, 0.760 at 2, 0.916 at 3, 0.975 at 4, 0.993 at 5, and 0.997 or higher from 6 to 8. On test, all 64 missed activations are small and carry 0.0% of the mass, mostly 0 inputs at steps 16-17 plus one d at step 17 that did fire but sits outside the copy phase (t=3 with L=9).

The early-copy silence looks like a graded magnitude cut off by the activation threshold, not a separate class of inputs. The share of predicted steps that fall in the lowest activation quartile drops with copy position (0.31 at recall_idx 1, 0.003 at 8, about 100x), and the predicate's correlation with the activation rises from 0.18 to about 0.40. So the claim that magnitude grows with copy position holds, although it was measured here per recall_idx rather than directly.

Minor gap: precision drops when d appears more than once in the original sequence and is fed back early in the copy phase (in_count >= 2 & recall_idx <= 2: precision 0.50 on 5692 steps). Carving this out barely changes the result (test F1 0.944 against 0.940), so it is a small refinement, not a systematic counterexample.
The silent steps are not explained by L, to_go, n_digits or neighbouring tokens: at recall_idx <= 2, precision stays between 0.71 and 0.84 across all of these splits.
